checks.claim: C1: The objects are the actual frozen family: real H_b=-d2-bU, U=Gamma*q with actual amplitude, fixed positive K, and F as the closure of compact smooth phases PLUS both constants in uniformly local E.
checks.reason: Sections 1 and 4 use the accepted ground and weighted objects, with M=||U||infinity carrying the amplitude. The projection and d come from those notes. No complement bound, single-bound-state or Riesz L1 premise appears. Infinitely many Riesz bound states are covered by the E2 convention.

checks.claim: C2: (2) B<=A_b<=cB holds with c=1+b1M, and both operators are >=1 with common form domain H1.
checks.reason: A_b=B+(b1M-bU) with 0<=b1M-bU<=b1M, and b1M<=b1M*B because B>=1. Hence A_b<=(1+b1M)B.

checks.claim: C2: The inverse variational formula and resolvent monotonicity hold for unbounded T,S.
checks.reason: Completing the square in the form norm of T+t gives <f,(T+t)^-1 f> minus the form norm of u-(T+t)^-1 f, with maximizer (T+t)^-1 f. Form order then gives the resolvent order and T/(T+t)<=S/(S+t) for each f in L2.

checks.claim: C2: The square-root integral, Tonelli step and domain inclusion yield (3).
checks.reason: The scalar integral is pi by the stated substitutions. Tonelli applied to the spectral measure of f gives <f,T^(1/2)f> in [0,infinity], so finiteness on the S side forces f in D(T^(1/4)). Applying this to (B,A_b) and (A_b,cB), with (cB)^(1/4)=c^(1/4)B^(1/4), gives (3) with the correct exponent and D(A_b^(1/4))=H1/2.

checks.claim: C2: The negative-dual completion and (4) identify E_b with E uniformly in b.
checks.reason: For w in L2, ||A^-1/4 w||=sup|<w,v>| over ||A^1/4 v||<=1, since A^1/4 maps its domain onto L2. Nesting the unit balls through (3) gives ||w||_A<=||w||_H-1/2<=c^(1/4)||w||_A. L2 is dense in H-1/2, the pairing is the distributional one, and c depends only on b1 and M.

checks.claim: C3: Q has spectral support in [-mu^2,infinity), and (5) is the correct wave matrix with the four stated conjugated entries.
checks.reason: Max-min with a simple isolated E1 gives the support. Differentiation gives u_t=-hS_t v+C_t w on each spectral branch, including h<0 and h=0. Conjugation by (A^1/4,A^-1/4) gives C_t, sqrt(h+c)S_t, -hS_t/sqrt(h+c) and C_t exactly.

checks.claim: C3: All four entries are <=C(1+t)exp(mu t) at positive, negative and zero h, with no inverse mu.
checks.reason: For h>=0, |S_t|<=min(t,h^-1/2) gives upper entry <=sqrt(1+c)(1+t) and lower entry <=1. For h<0, sinh(x)/x<=cosh(x) gives |S_t|<=t exp(mu t), and 1<=h+c<=c, |h|<=b1M follow from -mu^2>=E1>=-b1M. At mu=0 the negative case is vacuous and S_t(0)=t.

checks.claim: C3: The decaying ground branch is retained, the projections are uniform, and (6) follows.
checks.reason: For z=(v,w) with alpha=<p,v>, gamma=<p,w>, one has (I-Pi)z=(Qv,Qw)+a(p,-lambda p) with a=(alpha-gamma/lambda)/2, and the Q part is unaffected because ell vanishes on it. The branch evolves by exp(-lambda t)<=exp(mu t). Weighted norms use c-lambda^2 in [1,c] and l<=lambda<=L. The Q and branch parts are E_b-orthogonal, so (6) holds uniformly.

checks.claim: C3: The spectral flow equals the named physical flow on global E through H2xH1 regularity, Duhamel, uniqueness and density in E only.
checks.reason: For data in H2xH1 the multipliers give (u,u_t) in C(H2xH1), with u in C2(L2) and u_tt=-Hu. Differentiating S(t-s)z(s) gives the free Duhamel equation with forcing (0,bUu). Equality with the physical flow follows by Picard/Gronwall, which needs the small completion recorded in findings.minor, not a new idea. Extension uses density of compact smooth phases in E, E bounds for the spectral flow, F bounds for the physical flow and the E->F embedding. No density of E in F is used, and all E bounds come from the weighted calculus rather than L2 bounds.

checks.claim: C4: The kappa_(j,t) family exists with the stated radius and uniform derivatives, and (7) holds through a finite partition with an O(1+t) count.
checks.reason: A product of shifted fixed transitions equals 1 on [j-t-4,j+t+4], is supported in [j-t-5,j+t+5], and has derivative bounds independent of j and t. At most 2t+13 indices k contribute. Each term is bounded in E by a uniform W1infinity multiplier bound times ||chi_k z||_E. The triangle inequality gives (7), and kappa z is global E.

checks.claim: C4: Finite propagation holds on F including constants, and (8) follows.
checks.reason: The free group on F has the accepted localization identity, and bU multiplication preserves support. Picard terms converge factorially in F through accepted bounds on S on finite horizons and on B on F. Compact distributional testing is continuous. The input (1-kappa)z vanishes on |x-j|<t+4, so at time t its output vanishes on |x-j|<4, a set containing supp chi_j.

checks.claim: C4: Identity (9) is exact and has the correct sign.
checks.reason: Substituting R=P-exp(lambda t)e ell on both z and kappa z in (8) gives chi R z=chi R(kappa z)+exp(lambda t)chi e ell((kappa-1)z). Only the accepted P Pi=exp(lambda t)Pi is used.

checks.claim: C4: The local eigenvector bound ||chi_j e_b||_E<=C exp(-beta|j|) and the shifted dual bound (10) hold uniformly, including distant cells.
checks.reason: Pointwise tails of p and p' on |x|>=|j|-3 give the first bound. For (10), a cell k contributes only if |k-j|>=t+3, hence |k|>=t+3-|j|. Summing ||rho_k p||_H1<=C exp(-beta|k|) against the uniform multiplier bound gives C exp(-beta(t-|j|)) for t>|j|, and the full sum gives the uniform bound otherwise. The accepted centered bound (5) is not misapplied; the shifted cutoff is handled by rerunning the cell sum.

minor: Section 3 states the Picard/Gronwall uniqueness bound on global E, but the accepted physical flow is a priori F-valued. The conclusion still follows from accepted inputs in either of two ways. Run Gronwall on F using local-flow Section 5 bounds and the E->F embedding, or note that the physical flow of compact smooth data is compactly supported by finite propagation, hence global E with continuity from the local cutoff bounds. Stating the chosen space would be clearer; this is disclosed here, not silently absorbed.

The identification paragraph needs (5) on the full H_b spectrum, or an explicit exponential treatment of the p_b phase, whereas the displayed scalar bounds are stated on the Q support. The extension is immediate on finite horizons because h>=-lambda^2>=-b1M.

Real Hilbert spaces are used with the spectral theorem implicitly through complexification. This is harmless because the functional-calculus functions are real and H_b commutes with conjugation, but the note does not say so.
The derivation of (10) is compressed. The explicit cell condition |k|>=t+3-|j| and the geometric tail constant depending on beta would make the shifted estimate easier to audit.

Accepted internals of the ground, weighted-projection, local-flow and tilt notes were examined at their applications, as instructed, and not re-proved. This includes imported Teschl theorems, H1/2 multiplier bounds, free-group bounds on F, Young solution identities and admissibility of bU.

Packet-external files named in those notes were not read, including original source images and earlier reports. The target-v2 pre-proof source-crosswalk step and the audit records named by the adjudication could not be inspected, and were not treated as evidence.
